rationale: Weak fit: gold producer with no consumer brand and limited reason to sponsor F1.

desc: Japanese non-ferrous metals company mining and smelting copper, nickel and gold, and making battery materials for electric vehicles.
markets: Mines in Chile, Peru and Japan, with battery material sales to Asian carmakers and battery makers.
rationale: B2B supplier of battery cathode material; F1 hospitality could suit EV customers, but marketing culture is limited.

desc: London-headquartered gold miner operating mines in West Africa, selling gold to refiners and bullion markets.
markets: Mines in Cote d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, Senegal and Ghana; no consumer expansion plans.
rationale: Weak fit: gold producer with no consumer brand; F1 would only add investor visibility.

desc: Canadian gold miner with mines in Canada, Mexico and Turkey, selling gold to refiners and bullion markets.
markets: Mines in Canada, Mexico and Turkey; expansion at Island Gold and Magino projects.
rationale: Weak fit: mid-sized gold producer with no consumer brand and a limited marketing budget.

desc: US manufacturer of copper tube, fittings, brass rod and related products for plumbing, HVAC and industrial customers.
markets: Plants in the US, Mexico, the UK and Asia; customers are wholesalers and OEMs in North America.
rationale: Weak fit: industrial products maker selling to distributors and HVAC makers; F1 has limited relevance.

desc: Chinese gold miner producing gold and other metals from mines in Inner Mongolia and other regions, with overseas assets.
markets: Mines in China, with an overseas gold project; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Weak fit: regional gold miner with no consumer brand and no international marketing needs.

desc: Chinese lithium producer making lithium compounds for batteries, with mines in Australia, Argentina and Mali and a battery business.
markets: Lithium mines and projects in Australia, Argentina, Mali and Mexico; sells to battery and EV makers worldwide.
rationale: Lithium supplier to EV and battery makers; F1 offers technology tie-in with electrification and global B2B profile.

desc: Melbourne-based miner of copper and zinc owned by China Minmetals, with mines in Peru, Congo, Australia and Laos.
markets: Mines in Peru (Las Bambas), Congo, Australia and Laos; selling to smelters in Asia.
rationale: Weak fit: state-owned commodity producer; F1 could support Australian presence at the Melbourne Grand Prix, but there is no consumer brand.

desc: Indian diversified natural resources company producing zinc, aluminium, oil and gas, iron ore, steel and copper.
markets: Operations in India and Africa, with exports across Asia; planning to demerge into separate businesses.
rationale: Indian industrial group with growing consumer visibility could use F1 for brand prestige in India, though the resource-industry fit is weak.

desc: Aluminium producer mining bauxite, refining alumina and smelting aluminium for automotive, packaging, aerospace and construction customers.
markets: Operations in Australia, Brazil, Canada, Iceland, Norway and the US; low-carbon aluminium brands such as EcoSource.
rationale: Low-carbon aluminium for carmakers gives a technology and sustainability angle; F1 hospitality suits automotive B2B buyers.

desc: Australian steel company making coated and painted steel (Colorbond) and building products, with plants in Australia, the US, Asia.
markets: Operations in Australia, North America and Asia, including North Star BlueScope in Ohio; no verified further expansion.
rationale: Consumer-recognised Colorbond brand and Melbourne base could use F1 for brand building, but customers are mostly builders and distributors.

desc: Canadian gold miner with mines in Canada and West Africa, including the Cote Gold mine in Ontario.
markets: Mines in Canada and Burkina Faso; no consumer expansion plans.
rationale: Weak fit: mid-sized gold producer with no consumer brand and limited marketing budget.

desc: Steel producer with plants in Mexico, Brazil, Argentina and the US making flat and long steel for automotive and construction.
markets: Plants in Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia and the US; expansion in Mexico and Pesqueria.
rationale: Automotive steel supplier to Latin American plants; F1 hospitality, especially around Mexico and Brazil Grands Prix, could suit B2B customers.

desc: Canadian gold producer operating the Tocantinzinho mine in Brazil and developing the Oko West project in Guyana.
markets: Mine in Brazil and project in Guyana; no consumer expansion plans.
rationale: Weak fit: small gold producer with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship unaffordable and unrelated.

desc: South African producer of platinum group metals, mining in South Africa and Zimbabwe, selling to catalyst makers and industrial users.
markets: Mines in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Canada; sells platinum, palladium and rhodium to carmakers' catalyst suppliers.
rationale: Platinum group metals supply automotive catalysts, giving a tenuous tie to engineering audiences; F1 offers limited marketing value.

desc: Canadian copper miner with mines in Peru, Manitoba, Arizona and Nevada, selling copper concentrate and gold to smelters.
markets: Mines in Peru, Canada and the US; developing the Copper World project in Arizona.
rationale: Weak fit: mid-sized copper producer selling to smelters; F1 would offer limited relevance.

desc: South African gold miner operating mines in South Africa and Papua New Guinea, and copper-gold assets in Australia.
markets: Mines in South Africa, Papua New Guinea and Australia (Eva Copper); no consumer expansion plans.
rationale: Weak fit: gold producer with no consumer brand; F1 would add investor visibility only.

desc: Swedish steelmaker specialising in high-strength steels and fossil-free steel (HYBRIT), serving construction machinery, automotive and wear-plate customers.
markets: Plants in Sweden, Finland and the US; converting Nordic mills to fossil-free steel and expanding in Luleå.
rationale: Fossil-free steel and Hardox brand give a sustainability and technology showcase for carmakers and machinery makers; strong B2B hospitality fit.
